Specify duration-dependent union dissolution

Source: R/union_dissolution.R
union_dissolution.Rd

Constructs a union dissolution process specification for a simulation model. The convenience function set_union_dissolution is equivalent to set_process(model, union_dissolution(...)) and allows for direct piping from a model.

Usage

union_dissolution(rates, weights = NULL)

set_union_dissolution(model, rates, weights = NULL)

Arguments

rates

A nonempty data frame with at least numeric dur_start, dur_end, and rate. See details for format and description of stratification variables that can be applied.

weights

NULL (default) for unweighted selection, or a weight_model() using union variables, which chooses which union in a cell dissolves without changing the cell's input rate.

model

A hammel_model object.

Value

union_dissolution() returns an inspectable hammel_union_dissolution process with a tibble of rates; set_union_dissolution() returns an updated model.

Details

The primary and only required input to the function is a union dissolution rate schedule for the rates argument. This data frame must contain dur_start and dur_end columns to define the half-open age intervals (inclusive at the start and exclusive at the end) and a rate column for the duration-specific dissolution rates.

Rates are always specified as union dissolutions over union-years lived. Gaps in the duration band are treated as cases with zero rates.

Columns named by declared group dimensions (see set_groups()), such as race or region, supply separate schedules for each combination of their categories, but they must be suffixed by _h or _w to indicate the group of the husband or wife, respectively (e.g. race_h and race_w).

Optional time_start/time_end columns select half-open calendar intervals in absolute years, including fractional years. Both columns are required together; starts are finite and ends exceed starts (possibly Inf). Active slices must satisfy the strata and coverage rules and cover the requested simulation run.

If cohabitations are in use in the simulation, the rates can be stratified by union_type to supply both cohab and marriage schedules; without it the same duration risk applies to either type. The stratify_rates() function provides a quick means to add stratification to an existing rate schedule.

Examples

# Illustrative rates
diss_rates <- data.frame(
  dur_start = c(0, 5), dur_end = c(5, Inf),
  rate = c(0.04, 0.02)
)
model <- hammel_model() |> set_union_dissolution(diss_rates)
